events.continuity_hook: First planning session in the relationship; establishes a work-trip search where flight reliability and site timing matter more than airline loyalty.
events.interaction_goal: Build a concise flight-and-hotel shortlist that separates the strongest schedule from workable backups and flags what cannot be booked until the client confirms the demo delivery window.
events.scenario_brief: Jonah is planning a three-night client-site visit to a municipal water facility near Twin Falls, Idaho. He needs to leave the Bay Area on a Monday afternoon if workable, arrive in time for a Tuesday 7:30 a.m. security check-in, and return Thursday after a distributor lunch. SFO is easiest, Oakland is acceptable, and a single connection is fine if it is not risky. He also needs a hotel within about 20 minutes of the plant, with strong guest ratings, reliable early-morning logistics, in-room coffee and a mini-fridge if available, and nearby dinner options. The client has not yet confirmed whether a demo crate delivery will require him to arrive earlier.

events.continuity_hook: Follows the Twin Falls search after the client tightened the arrival schedule and made the original Monday-afternoon plan less comfortable.
events.interaction_goal: Revise the shortlist around the earlier site-access time, compare the cost and schedule trade-off of arriving Sunday versus Monday, and identify the option worth approving.
events.scenario_brief: The client moves the Tuesday site access earlier to 6:45 a.m. and adds a Monday evening supplier dinner in Boise. Jonah now wants to compare keeping a Monday outbound against adding a Sunday night hotel stay, with priority on avoiding a late-night drive after landing. The hotel search should be narrowed to properties that can handle an early departure from the lobby and have straightforward parking. The remaining unresolved item is whether the extra hotel night needs manager approval.

events.continuity_hook: Completes the first work-trip episode after the refinement made Sunday arrival the safer schedule.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the flight and hotel booking details, capture seat and room requests, and produce a clean confirmation summary for Jonah to forward internally.
events.scenario_brief: Jonah receives approval for the extra night and is ready to book the Twin Falls trip. The selected plan is a Sunday afternoon Bay Area departure into Boise with enough daylight for the drive, a Thursday mid-afternoon return, and a well-rated Twin Falls hotel near the client site. He wants the room notes to include coffee maker and mini-fridge confirmation, and he wants a window seat selected if available. The only remaining loose end is sending the arrival time and hotel address to the client coordinator.

events.continuity_hook: New episode after the Idaho client trip; shifts from a site-visit schedule to conference logistics with hotel-location trade-offs.
events.interaction_goal: Compare conference-area hotel options against the official block and outline flight choices for both a solo Sunday arrival and a Saturday arrival if the personal weekend is added.
events.scenario_brief: Jonah starts planning for a water-technology conference in Seattle with booth setup on Sunday afternoon, sessions Monday through Wednesday, and a possible customer dinner Tuesday night. He needs flights from the Bay Area and a hotel that works for early booth access, either in the official block or within a practical walk or short ride of the convention center. The official block is convenient but expensive, and he is unsure whether his spouse will join for the weekend before the conference, which affects the outbound date and seating approach.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Seattle conference episode after the personal-weekend uncertainty drops away and the hotel block becomes less attractive.
events.interaction_goal: Narrow the trip to a solo conference booking, choose between the remaining hotel options, and select flights that protect the booth setup and teardown schedule.
events.scenario_brief: Jonah confirms his spouse will not join the Seattle trip, so the plan narrows to a solo business itinerary. The official hotel block has only high-rate rooms left, and he wants a nearby alternative with a better value while still keeping the Wednesday return late enough to avoid rushing after booth teardown. A United schedule is competitive, but he is open to another carrier if the departure or return timing is cleaner. Hotel rating, commute to the convention center, and cancellation terms are the main unresolved comparisons.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new short-notice work episode after the Seattle conference planning, with schedule certainty outweighing normal comparison depth.
events.interaction_goal: Find and book a workable flight-and-hotel package quickly, prioritizing arrival reliability, one-connection routing, and a hotel that supports an early training day.
events.scenario_brief: A distributor training in the Cedar Rapids area changes from virtual to in person with little notice. Jonah needs to leave the Bay Area the next afternoon if possible, arrive with enough time to review demo materials, train the distributor team the following morning, and return the day after the training. He wants to avoid multiple connections, keep the hotel near the industrial park rather than downtown, and find a room with practical work-trip basics plus dinner options nearby. Because the training slot is fixed, the trip may need to be booked in one session even if the fare is not ideal.
